title: Hopscotch, hide and seek, and silent movie theater pits
summary: Children's games and silent films with a pit pianist; Albert played in a theater pit with bassist Tolles as a kid; tape runs out.

venues.name: Silent movie theater on Washington Street

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Well of course, it's easy to get two sides of the same story. I mean if one man tells it one way and another one tells it that way. But both the truth is each man sees it. Right. He never did. Oh, back to the kids games. Did you ever play hopscotch?
Yeah, sure. That was with the gals. The gals played hopscotch. Yeah, right. We'd draw the hopscotch for them on the sidewalk.
So you had little girlfriends around there. Oh yeah, sure. And they'd do all that kind of stuff.
Yeah, hopscotch was that game. Yeah. And hide and seek, you'd run and hide and then you'd hit a can and say one, two, three, I spy so and so and you'd have to tell them where you're spying.
And he's it.
The guy who's it hits a can. Right.
Did you ever hear the game of Rockette? That might be from before your time.
Maybe we're not saying the right word to Rockette.

No, Rockette. Rockette. They had a Rockette field back on Allegiant Field Avenue. No, I don't think so. I used to hear about it I think from guys back in the 1890s. But the game died. It was like lacrosse. Yeah, no.
I never knew it.
I think it must have been an Indian game that got brought to New Orleans. Right. Oh, you mentioned the movies then. They were silent when you were young?
That's right. Silent creatures.
Well, what kind of noise did they have? Did they have anything?
Well, there wasn't any noise. None at all. Look at the thing there, turning over the film. Didn't have any piano player?
Sometimes, yeah.
Sometimes they had a piano player in the pit.
Anything more than a piano player?
Well, I remember the time his theater way up on Washington. I can't remember the name, but I played in the pit with an old guy named Tolles. He was a bass player.
Oh, yeah. Not Tolles' daddy properly, huh? It was not himself.
Oh, not.
Not Tolles, huh?

Yeah. And he played in the pit during the intermission. Then the pitch would come back on and the band just started to play again. A lot of times in the... Well, that's why Eddie Hewitt's daddy was in Atlanta, Georgia, a pit piano player. Oh, the tape's about to run out. Let me get a little... Is that up?
